comparison.objective: PR-1570 closes an adjustable wrench snugly on a nylon nut, loosens the nut in the safe direction, and sets the wrench down; the candidate sets and locks an opening-stop screw on a gripper.
comparison.physical_skill: PR-1570 tests thumbwheel adjustment, jaw-clearance control, correct fixed-jaw loading, breakaway pulling, and tool removal; the candidate tests coaxial driver seating plus simultaneous wrench seating and countertorque to prevent setting drift.
comparison.success_condition: PR-1570 grades loosened angle, loose-jaw and wrong-direction faults, wrench set-down, and release; the candidate grades angular accuracy, jam-nut seating, repeated retained motion, stop drift, hardware retention, and clearance.
comparison.reason: The shared wrench-and-nut primitive is insufficient for overlap because PR-1570 tests adjustable-wrench fit and pull direction, whereas the candidate tests coupled two-tool lockup without disturbing a setting; no material rubric detail is missing.
